findings.text: non-blocking: the Gate paragraph reports '85 passed, 4 failed, 0:02:14, EXIT=1 ... on the committed tree', but the reviewed head's own gate log logs/gate-round4.log names revision 3149f9b6f and reports 87 passed, 4 failed, 0:01:42; the 85 figure is gate-coordinator.log's, whose header names 2abb60a10, a revision that does not hold the two cases added after it. The command quoted is also abbreviated ('PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest ...') rather than the literal twelve-target command the log records, so the plan's 'the evidence fragment quotes each gate's command and summary line' is not met for the head gate. The code is not in doubt — the head gate exists and passes — but the record points a reader at the wrong reading.

non-blocking: the Negative control paragraph says the mutation was run 'against the committed tree', while logs/negative-control.log's own header names revision bef70cb4, an earlier revision of this node's tree; the mutated run-ended branch (reckon/crew/gc.py:1216-1219) is unchanged at the head, so the result transfers, but the sentence as written is not what the log records and a reader cannot tell whether the control was re-applied to the code being promoted.

non-blocking: negative_control_log names logs/negative-control-repair.log, whose mutation withdraws the coherence guard (1 failed, 10 deselected), not the declared control 'a settling pass that keeps the orphan sweep's age wait ... the second-host case must fail', whose log is logs/negative-control.log (3 failing ids including the second-host case). Admission still reads a red log with a failing id the head arm does not fail, so the record is not refused, but the field names a log that does not answer the control the node declared.

non-blocking: _run_directory_records_end writes the record names as literals ('exit.json', 'discard.json') although reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1741 defines EXIT_RECORD_NAME and reckon/crew/promotion.py:1798 defines DISCARD_RECORD_NAME; a rename of either record leaves the settling pass reading a name nothing writes and silently treating finished runs as unended.

justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/gc.py:1031 is now the single owner of the coherent-root rule and both passes call it, but the record names at gc.py:1171-1173 repeat literals that reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1741 and reckon/crew/promotion.py:1798 already declare.
